title: The Cone Line
hook: Cones walk left. Two yellow coats wait past the taper.
scene: Overcast morning on the Ribbon. You have not left the freeway. Orange cones walk left across the right lane, stepping toward the skip-dash; two workers in hi-viz wait past the taper. The left still looks like a clean number. The gantry overhead is blank. If you carry highway leftover through people on the deck, the cones will not catch you.
decision: The work zone is already taking the right. What do you do?

options.text: Move early: bleed speed now and take the shift before the cones close the right
options.result: You dump the leftover before the crew. When the cones finish the pinch, you are already in the lane they leave you. The workers stay workers. The Beetle stays a car in a zone, not a problem in one.

options.text: Hold highway speed and force the leftover through the taper
options.result: You keep the leftover. The workers do not move. A cone line is not a suggestion. You write a highway number through a place that already asked for less.

options.text: Brake hard at the taper when the cones finish the pinch
options.result: You wait until the pinch is a wall, then stand on it. The car behind you still has leftover. The crew did not ask for a panic stop in their taper.

debrief: In a marked work zone, slow down and take the lane shift early. Do not hold leftover speed or brake at the pinch. You lost the leftover before the shift.

source.psdp_skill: Skill eleven: highway driving – part one
source.teaching_target: Work zone: reduce speed and take the lane shift early. Do not hold highway leftover or brake hard at the taper.
